scope: Two R51 interim FoSCoS edible dried seeds source routes reconciled with FSSAI signed order 15 Mar 2024; no actual seed grade, FSSR standard, CTR legal article or commercial approval.

records.product_name: Edible Dried Seeds obtained from Fruits
blockers: Identify precise botanical species, legal seed origin/part, intended edible grade and source food category; commodity identity cannot be inferred from the 'fruits' or 'vegetables' umbrella alone
Confirm whole, dried, salted, roasted, powdered, sprouted, oil-extracted or other manufactured state before invoking a named FSSR/CTR article
Reconcile current original notifications, any post-2024 product-specific standards and FoSCoS product listing against the 2024 interim order
Assess actual lot, supplier, formulation/carriers, allergen/cross-contact risks, microbiological hazards and full applicable metal/mycotoxin/pesticide panel with matrix-validated methods
Verify license and food-business type, registered product route, actual test evidence and approved internal independent legal review
non_inheritance_rules: Do not equate a seed commodity to the whole fruit or vegetable flesh article for pesticides/metals without legally correct commodity/matrix definition
Do not transfer peanut, tree-nut, sesame, pulse, hemp, cumin or sunflower raw source MRLs solely because a product is called edible seeds
Do not use the 2024 source to claim a distinct safety standard, a regulatory exemption, an actual edible grade, or automatic batch release

global_guards: March 2024 statement of no specific standard applies to the order's publication date; it is not proof that no standard could have been notified afterwards.
The 4.1.2.2 versus 4.2.2.2 source route alone cannot identify actual seed species or commodity-specific contaminants.
Watermelon-seed request is context, not an automatic species assignment to either of the two generic catalogue records.
Seeds, oil, powder, seedlings meant for planting, and seed-derived ingredients may be different products requiring different classification.
FSSAI category is a licensing authorization channel, not commercial approval or a replacement for current CTR/MRL, microbiological, labelling and actual source-testing requirements.
